To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

phishing counter measures can be classified into the following eight categories: (1) server-side security indicators (2) client-side toolbars (3) client-side warnings (4) client-side security certificates (5) client-side black lists (6) client-side white lists (7) client-side security software (8) client-side security education.
there are many phishing countermeasures proposed in literature, however, there is no clear indication that any of these countermeasures is effective in preventing the phishing attacks.

the current anti phishing approaches that have seen considerable deployments over the internet are classified into eight categories, namely, user education and awareness, server-side security indicators, client-side toolbars, warnings and alerts, browser-based anti-phishing solutions, anti-phishing plugins, anti-phishing software, and anti-spam solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of anti-phishing countermeasures and the effectiveness of the existing anti-phishing counter measures.
the identification and evaluation of the available anti-phishing approaches and the development of a framework to guide researchers in their future work on phishing countermeasures.
the identification of the research gaps that are prevailing in this field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no silver bullet to prevent phishing attacks and that a combination of the available countermeasure is required to achieve the desired level of security.
the research on phishing and its counter measures is not yet matured enough.
the existing anti-phishing measures and techniques have failed to provide a satisfactory solution to the problem of phishing and further research is needed in this field.

phishing is a serious issue that is not going away any time soon.
there is a need to develop a new approach for phishing detection that can detect the phishing websites in the very early stages of their existence.
phishing is a very serious threat to internet users, which can lead to the loss of money and/or confidential information.

there is still a long way to go before we can say that phishing is a solved problem.
